messages:
maria (Customer Success): Hey team — customer TIMCorp on a private deployment is seeing their invoice for Feb show ~15% more tokens than our audit ledger. ticket CS-9281. They insist their on-prem audit logs match the gateway totals, but our billing ledger is higher.

tim (Customer): Confirming. Our gateway logs (sha256: a3f4...) and local audit report 1,250,412 tokens. Invoice shows 1,439,020 tokens billed.

maria (Customer Success): Repro steps from the customer: they run the agent on a single vm behind a VPC, agent version 1.9.2, with offline_buffer_size=20000, flush_interval=30s. They had a maintenance window 2025-02-12 03:00 UTC with high disk I/O.

nish (Support): Thanks. First guess: agent offline buffer overflow or duplicate replay after restart. Can you ask them for the agent status output and last 200 lines of /var/log/redwood/meter-agent.log? Also we need the agent config + checksum.

tim (Customer): Pasting snippets: 
```
$ cat /etc/redwood/meter-agent.conf
version = "1.9.2"
offline_buffer_size = 20000
flush_interval = 30
seq_mode = "monotonic"
```
And tail of log: 
```
2025-02-12T02:59:58Z INFO buffer size reached 20000, persisting to disk
2025-02-12T03:00:12Z WARN disk write latency 512ms
2025-02-12T03:00:15Z INFO restart initiated by systemd
2025-02-12T03:00:17Z INFO replaying buffer, events=20004
2025-02-12T03:00:18Z ERROR seqid wrap detected: last=4294967294, next=2
2025-02-12T03:00:18Z INFO replay complete, delivered=20004
```

bryce (SRE-oncall): seqid wrap detected + replay of ~20k events during a restart looks suspicious. If agent uses 32-bit seqid, wrap could cause duplicate seq ids after restart and downstream service may count them twice depending on dedupe window.

meter-agent-bot: (automated) agent-metrics: {"uptime_s":"3600","queued_events":"0","replayed_events":"20004","last_seq":"2","seq_space":"wrap"}

nish (Support): Two parallel hypotheses: 1) replay was accepted twice by the collector (duplicate delivery) because client-side dedupe metadata truncated on wrap; 2) ledger truncation on local audit caused audit logs to miss older events (so ledger appears lower). Need to compare raw envelope hashes between customer audit and our ingest ledger for the window around 03:00 UTC.

leo (Billing): From billing side I can confirm invoice totals match the ingest ledger we have: 1,439,020 tokens. Need engineering verification of duplicates before we consider adjustments.

maria (Customer Success): I'm asking the customer to upload the audit slice and the agent persisted buffer file (they agreed). Ticket updated with S3 link: s3://cs-uploads/CS-9281/agent-buffer.tar.gz (restricted).

bryce (SRE-oncall): Action plan:
1) Support to fetch agent persisted buffer and run dedupe tool locally: `rdw-meter dedupe --buffer agent-buffer.bin --out hashes.txt`
2) Eng to diff hashes.txt vs our ingest ledger for seq range 4,294,967,290 -> 4,294,967, + wrap -> 2 (window 02:59:50-03:01:00).
3) If duplicates found, determine if dedupe at collector failed (look for X-Redwood-Dedupe header) or collector ack mismatch.

nish (Support): I ran `rdw-meter dedupe` on the provided buffer. Quick grep: 
```
$ grep -c "duplicate-hash" hashes.txt
19784
```
So ~19.8k duplicates present in the buffer.

bryce (SRE-oncall): That aligns with replayed_events. Next: check our ingest service acks for that time window. Can eng-runtime pull logs from collector-az1 for 2025-02-12T03:00:00->03:05:00, grep for X-Redwood-Dedupe header and for client seq ids?

leo (Billing): If duplicates are confirmed and were billed, billing will need an adjustment. Please include the exact token delta and list of duplicate request-ids so we can create a credit.

meter-agent-bot: (automated) ledger-query: {"start_ts":"2025-02-12T02:59:50Z","end_ts":"2025-02-12T03:01:00Z","tokens_billed":188608,"tokens_unique":168720}

nish (Support): meter-bot result shows billed - unique = 19,888 tokens (close to duplicate count). Need per-request id list. Requesting eng-runtime to export `request_id,token_count,seq` for that window from ingest ledger.

bryce (SRE-oncall): Also flag: agent uses 32-bit unsigned seq which wrapped. Immediate mitigation: update agent to 1.10.0 which uses 64-bit seq and safe replay semantics. Patch release has been marked urgent.

maria (Customer Success): Customer ok with temporary credit while we confirm. They prefer a formal RCA and will require timeline and fix.

nish (Support): Filing ENG ticket ENG-5642 to extract per-request ids and confirm dedupe status. Posting relevant logs to the eng channel and will ping when ready.

tim (Customer): Thanks, appreciate the quick turnaround. Any ETA for the credit?

leo (Billing): If eng confirms duplicates, we can apply a pro-rated credit within 3 business days. I'll hold until ENG-5642 sig-off.

bryce (SRE-oncall): Interim workaround posted to internal KB: run `sysctl -w vm.swappiness=10` and increase offline_buffer_size or enable persistent seq metadata across restarts. Long-term: force 64-bit seq and add wrap detection alerts.

nish (Support): Closing loop: next steps assigned in CS ticket CS-9281, ENG-5642 opened, billing on standby. Will update thread when ledger extract arrives. :thumbsup:
